messages:
devon: quick note 1 - on latest int8 bring-up (sable-liteq) canary were seeing ~5.4% structured funcall parse failures vs 0.3% fp32. distribution skew toward streaming responses. :thinking_face:
maya: ack. any concrete artifact (chunk dumps, raw bytes)?
devon: uploaded dumps to INF-3301. snippet shows weird separators and occasional 0x00 between objects: 
```
...}\u0000
{\"name\":\"search\",\"args\":{\"q\":\"tokens\"}}
```
aj: that 0x00 + newline combo will confuse our NDJSON parser if chunk boundaries split differently. seems quant path shifted tokenization/emit timing.
ryan: streaming aggregator assumes newline-delimited JSON per object. if a chunk contains an embedded control char we either buffer or mis-parse. can we see if KV cache prefixing adds padding?
maya: good call. could be kvcache padding or a micro-optimization in the quantized emit kernel adding sentinel bytes. I'm adding a wrapper to log trailing bytes pre-flush in the next runtime build.
lina: from product side we need to know user impact. is this limited to toolcall flows only? conversation or generation endpoints affected?
devon: mostly toolcall flows; regular text gen OK. toolcall schema + streaming NDJSON is the common path.
aj: short-term mitigation proposal: implement a canary-only streaming sanitizer that: (1) normalizes lone control bytes (NULL, RS, etc.) to \n, (2) buffers until a full top-level JSON object is detected, (3) coalesces multiple top-level objects into NDJSON emission instead of failing. every repair emits metric `struct_repair.count` and logs original raw chunk.
maya: pseudo implementation for aggregator: 
```
buf += chunk
buf = buf.replace('\u0000','\n').replace('\u001e','\n')
while has_complete_top_object(buf): obj, buf = pop_next_top_object(buf)
emit(obj)
# keep remainder buffered
```
ryan: important: don't silently mask corruptions. sanitizer must increment `struct_repair` and attach `repair_detail` to trace. keep strict mode for prod.
lina: timeline / rollout plan? we want to ship a conservative patch quickly to reduce user-facing failures for canary customers, but not prod.
devon: propose: maya lands sanitizer PR by EOD; aj will wire a split canary (50/50 patched vs baseline) tomorrow AM; canary runs collect `parse_failure.rate` and `struct_repair.count`. if repair rate < 1% and no silent data corruption pattern, we keep investigating runtime changes. if repair rate > 1.5% escalate kernel team.
aj: also need a deterministic repro harness. devon can export chunk dumps; I'll convert to unit tests that feed exact chunk boundaries to the streaming parser to prevent regressions.
maya: will also add tokenization snapshots to canary traces (`token_boundary.bytes`) so we can map token indices -> byte offsets. that will help root-causing whether tokenization moved boundary or kernel emitted padding.
ryan: one more heuristic: if a chunk ends with a UTF-8 incomplete sequence, buffer until next chunk rather than attempting to parse. may reduce false positives.
devon: Ill run a repro pipeline: `rdw canary run --id 6345-repro --model sable-liteq --seed 7 --trace-stream --dump-chunks --dump-tokens` and attach to INF-3301.
ops-bot: created ticket INF-3301 "int8 streaming parser failures: chunk-sentinel investigation" and attached current dumps.
canary-bot: scheduled split canary 634567 for 09:00 PT tomorrow. good luck :rocket:
aj: follow-ups assigned: maya -> sanitizer PR + unit tests, devon -> dump export + repro, ryan -> token trace instrumentation, lina -> user impact summary and postmortem doc outline. well sync in #eng-ml after first canary run metrics are in.
